title: Circulatory Transport and Clearance: Hemodynamics, Renal Filtration, and Hepatic Clearance from the Jamming Substrate
abstract: The kidney and liver are emerged from measured human master-gene promoter DNA (SIX2, HHEX stacking energy gamma; SantaLucia 1998, never fitted); from them a full transport-clearance physiology (MAP=CO*SVR, Windkessel tau=RC, GFR autoregulation, osmoregulation, hepatic first-pass clearance), 14 disease states and a shared R19 carcinogen dose-response follow deterministically across 23 reproducible targets.
headline_results: aflatoxin x HBV: additive decrements => multiplicative RR (~72 vs 73)

chapters.owner_note: Isolated systolic hypertension is owned by the homeostasis_hemodynamic sibling (a regulated pressure-setpoint disorder); its structural driver, central arterial stiffening, is an aging_senescence process. chapters.title: Chronic kidney disease and GFR staging
chapters.owner_note: Ownership decided (handoff §4.4, v0.5.0): chronic kidney disease is not circulatory-owned. It is the downstream final-common-pathway readout of sibling etiologies — diabetic and hypertensive nephropathy owned by the homeostasis siblings, and intrinsic age-related nephron loss owned by aging_senescence. Circulatory retains this section only as a demonstration of its renal autoregulation relation (total GFR = surviving-nephron fraction × the autoregulated per-nephron value), not as a circulatory-owned disease.

chapters.owner_note: The injury here — glomerular hypertension — is driven by systemic hypertension owned by the homeostasis_hemodynamic sibling. Shown here only as a perturbation of circulatory's renal autoregulation plateau — a boundary demonstration, not a circulatory-owned disease.

cross_references.entity: von Hippel-Lindau disease / hereditary clear-cell renal cell carcinoma
cross_references.variant: germline loss-of-function (autosomal dominant); >300 pathogenic variants across 3 exons
cross_references.function: VHL is the substrate-recognition subunit of an E3 ubiquitin-ligase that degrades HIF-alpha under normoxia
cross_references.mechanism: germline VHL loss + somatic second hit -> constitutive HIF-alpha (esp. HIF-2alpha) stabilisation -> clear-cell RCC; ~2-4% of all RCC is VHL-syndrome familial, and somatic VHL inactivation is the initiating event in >90% of sporadic clear-cell RCC
cross_references.ownership_clause: MASTER MAP 6.1 -- monogenic gene-key entities are owned by the rare-disease volume
cross_references.circulatory_owned_sibling_section: 22 (renal cancer roster: acquired carcinogens on the kidney R19 axis)
cross_references.seam_to_circulatory: trichloroethylene -- a circulatory-owned ACQUIRED RCC carcinogen placed on the kidney R19 axis in section 22 -- exerts its renal genotoxicity through the SAME VHL/HIF pathway whose germline loss defines hereditary RCC. The acquired drive axis (22) and the germline gene-key entity (disease_wp) therefore meet at VHL: one is an exogenous sustained drive, the other a heritable predisposing loss of the same gatekeeper.
cross_references.anchor: VHL maps to 3p25-26; germline VHL -> VHL disease with clear-cell RCC (NCI PDQ, Genetics of VHL Syndrome); pVHL/HIF axis and >90% sporadic somatic inactivation (Kaelin, Clin Cancer Res 2004;10(18):6290s-6295s; 2007;13(2):680s)
cross_references.grade: [V] identity + seam (barrier-height derivation owned by disease_wp; gamma^2/4 grounding [O]/[H])

chapters.title: Liver cancer: the carcinogen roster, synergy, and prevention

cross_references.variant: p.C282Y (c.845G>A; Cys282Tyr) homozygous in ~80-90% of phenotypic HH; H63D contributes mainly as C282Y/H63D compound heterozygosity (autosomal recessive)
cross_references.function: HFE regulates hepcidin-mediated control of intestinal iron absorption
cross_references.mechanism: HFE loss -> unregulated iron absorption -> total-body and hepatic iron overload -> cirrhosis -> HCC. Male-predominant (women partly protected by menstrual iron loss).
cross_references.ownership_clause: MASTER MAP 6.1 -- monogenic gene-key entities are owned by the rare-disease volume
cross_references.circulatory_owned_sibling_section: 23 (liver cancer roster: acquired carcinogens on the liver R19 axis)
cross_references.seam_to_circulatory: iron-overload cirrhosis is a chronic injury drive on the SAME liver R19 axis that carries circulatory's acquired HCC carcinogens (aflatoxin / HBV / HCV / ethanol) in section 23. The germline HFE entity supplies a heritable, ENDOGENOUS predisposing drive that the acquired carcinogen roster otherwise treats as exogenous -- the same final-common cell-fate barrier, reached from a gene-key rather than an exposure. A documented iron x alcohol synergy (Scotet 2003; Asare 2008) is the haemochromatosis-context analogue of the section-23 multiplicative-synergy result, owned with the gene-key by disease_wp.
cross_references.anchor: Atkins JL et al., JAMA 2020;324(20):2048-2057, doi:10.1001/jama.2020.21566, PMID 33231665 -- UK Biobank: male C282Y homozygotes hazard ratio 10.5 (95% CI 6.6-16.7) for primary hepatic malignancy; lifetime risk to age 75 = 7.2% vs 0.6% for men with neither variant; no significant association in women
cross_references.grade: [V] identity + cited magnitude (HR 10.5) + seam (barrier-height derivation owned by disease_wp; gamma^2/4 grounding [O]/[H])
